chunks: And from him, from Ahmad, from al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Fadalah ibn Ayyub, from al-Husayn ibn 'Uthman, from 'Amr ibn Abi Nasr, who said:
I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him): 'Is it permissible for a man to speak during the Adhan?' He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no harm / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to speak during the Adhan in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that speaking during the Adhan is permissible (la ba'sa), distinguishing it from the recommended etiquette of silence and attentiveness. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding the Adhan, where the call serves as a public announcement rather than a strictly binding ritual requiring absolute quiet, provided the speaker does not disrupt the caller or the congregation significantly. The permissibility underscores the functional role of the Adhan as a notification mechanism within the broader framework of prayer obligations.
